the DEMO model is now able to: (1) explicitly specify measures of an organization’s critical properties; (2) specify viability norms, that are restrictions on these measures’ values; and (3) define resilience strategies, that are defined as a sequence of actions to control and eliminate dysfucntions, that are violations of viability norms.
we have developed a proposal for a new model for DEMO that allows for the explicit specification of viability norms, dysfunctions and resilience strategies.

the Control Organization Model (COM) extends DEMO to enable: (1) the specification of viability norms and dysfunctions and (2) the specification of resilience strategies that control dysfunctions and restore the organization’s viability norms.

the specification, in DEMO, of the critical properties of an organizational system and the specification of strategies to control and eliminate the dysfunctions that may occur in the system.
the development and validation of a formal model of organizational viability, dysfunctions and resilience strategies.
the viability and resilience of organizations, which are critical to their success.

the proposed extension of DEMO to a Control Organization Model is a significant contribution to the DEMO project, which can now be used in practice for a more precise specification of the viability and resilience of an organization.

our proposal extends DEMO with an ontological model that can be used to specify the organization as a whole and its properties – measures, viability norms and dysfunctions – and the resilience strategies that can be employed to control and eliminate them.
we have proposed an extension to DEMO that enables it to explicitly model an organization’s viability norms, dysfunctions and resilience strategies.

we have developed a model to specify the control mechanisms of an organization that are necessary to ensure its viability.
we now have a model that allows us to specify an organization as a system of inter-related measures, viability norms and resilience strategies.
with our proposal DEMO can now also be used to model the viability of organizations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DEMO is now able to model the viability of an organization and to specify resilience strategies for eliminating dysfunctions that may occur in an organization.
DEMO can now explicitly model the viability norms and resilience strategies of organizations.
DEMO is now a suitable tool to specify and reason about the viability of an organization, and the strategies that can be used to maintain the viability of the organization.
